newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia mine sees 93,000 oz gold output in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia mine sees 93,000 oz gold output in 1996.

text.p: PT Newmont Minahasa Raya's Minahasa gold mine in Indonesia's Northern Sulawesi is expected to produce 93,000 ounces of gold during its first nine months of operation this year, a top official said on Wednesday.

"The first gold was poured on the last day of March and we are processing 2,000 tonnes a day of ore averaging 7.11 grammes per tonne," the company's president director Tom Mair told Reuters in an interview.
The mine is expected to average production of about 140,000 ounces a year over its 13-year lifespan based on existing reserves.
PT Newmont Minahasa Raya is 80 percent owned by the U.S. Newmont Gold Company through Newmont Indonesia Ltd and 20 percent by an Indonesian mining company, PT Tanjung Serapung.
The mine is located 100 km south of the North Sulawesi provincial capital of Manado, near the coastal village of Ratatotok less than one degree north of the equator.
Construction on the $132 million project started in October 1994 and production began last March.
Eric Hamer, vice-president of Newmont Gold Co, said current reserves amounted to 8.8 million tonnes of ore at 7.1 grammes a tonne with an anticipated 90 percent recovery rate.
"We are still actively exploring in the area and hope to find more reserves," he added.
The plant is currently processing oxide ore and will start processing refactory ore when a circulating fluid bed roaster is commissioned early next year.

Hamer said the mine was using under-sea disposal for its tailings which are discharged from a 1,080-metre pipeline on a slope at a depth of 82 metres, the first time this technique has been used in Indonesia.
